beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. This is how Walker is meant to be asked: hand it a game design document, get back a playable Godot project. The prompt on screen is a reconstruction, not a transcript, because this game was rebuilt first, and its document came after.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a first-person puzzle game — a space station folded into two layers, energy cells carried between machines, and an unstable core taken past two guardians — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: What happened: a Unity puzzle game with no levels was rebuilt in Godot first.
GDD.md was written afterwards, from the evidence.

show.event: ClaudeComposerAsk: The Design Document

beats.narration_text: Delta came before its design document. Unity left sixty-four scripts and a kit of art, but no levels, scenes or sound. The rebuild made all twelve levels. The document was written last, and nothing in it is signed off.

props.text:
Delta
was built from its GDD.
Nothing is signed off.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant writer: text is typed on screen over the narration, so mid-beat samples legitimately show a partial page. The finished six-line text fills the safe area and holds for the last 1.5 s.

beats.narration_text: The document separates six kinds of claim: recovered from the Unity code, invented for the rebuild, built, observed, proposed, or still waiting on a person. Built: twenty-seven scripts and three shaders. Observed: the game's playtest passes, and ninety assertions pass in this film's four scripted takes. Human playtests: zero.

beats.narration_text: The vision is a proposal: fold yourself between two layers of a broken station, carry energy where it's needed, and walk the unstable core to the stabiliser. Who it's for is left open. The pillars are read off the code: one floor plan in two layers, energy as a thing you carry, and a narrator who teaches while the level tests.

beats.narration_text: Here's the core loop on the real build, played by a script, not a person. The level banner. Look at a cell, and F picks it up. Look at the socket, and E plugs it in. The door opens, the lift ends the level, and the panel shows the time. Every step is a cut from one take, in order.

beats.narration_text: Four experience goals, all proposed, each with a test a person has to run. The captures can only hint. The script cleared all twelve levels without dying. But it knows every solution in advance, and it read the guardian's timers instead of the warnings. That's not a first-time player.

beats.narration_text: Shifting is Unity's dimension switcher: a glitch up, fifty metres up or down with whatever you hold, and a glitch down. The rebuild adds one rule. If the other layer has no floor there, or something solid is in the way, the shift is refused. Unity would have left you stuck in a wall.

beats.narration_text: Unity's health manager reloads the scene on death, and its respawn trigger catches falls. The rebuild keeps both: fall off a deck and you're back at the checkpoint, a fallen cell goes home, and plasma or a guardian strike restarts the level.

beats.narration_text: The guardians keep Unity's timing: the first attack at seventeen seconds, then every twenty. A strike's sparks follow you for five seconds, lock, and three seconds later lightning kills within three metres. A shockwave ring must be jumped. The level around them is the rebuild's: two generators, a vault, a shield.

beats.narration_text: The biggest gap: Unity delivered no levels at all. All twelve are text maps on a five metre grid, built at runtime from the modular kit. Each introduces one idea, from a single socket in Cold Start to two guardians in Delta.

beats.narration_text: Menus port Unity's pause menu, options and scene loader, and add Continue, Select level with best times, and Credits. The pause menu lists R to restart and N to skip. Both are broken, and so is the mouse.

beats.narration_text: Escape pauses. A mouse click on Resume does nothing: a full-screen container for the options panel sits on top of the buttons. Arrows and Enter work. R, pressed while paused, does nothing too: the level node is paused with everything else. The menu's own Restart level works.

beats.narration_text: The world is the kit on a five metre grid: indoor floors with lamps and windows onto space, outdoor decks with rails and asteroids. Upper Delta is cool, Lower Delta warm. The art is the Unity project's. The sound isn't: Unity had an audio manager and no audio files, so thirty-three effects and three music tracks were synthesized, and VEGA is subtitles.

portrait_card.reason: native 9:16 large-type card; shared 916 board fine print is below the GATE T portrait floor

show.event: portrait card: Kit Art, Synthesized Sound

beats.narration_text: Under the hood, every level scene is one node running one script with a level number; the station, devices and power links are built from the text map. Out of scope, by decision: Unity's outline highlights and audio-reactive effects, and voiced narration.

portrait_card.reason: native 9:16 large-type card; shared 916 board fine print is below the GATE T portrait floor
portrait_card.title: One Node per Level

show.event: portrait card: One Node per Level

beats.narration_text: The risks section is candid. The captures found what the game's own test missed: the pause menu ignores clicks, its keys are dead while paused, a player on a moving shuttle creeps forward, and Continue logs an engine error. The playtest never paused, and steered the player directly. Five questions remain for a person.

portrait_card.reason: native 9:16 large-type card; shared 916 board fine print is below the GATE T portrait floor
portrait_card.title: What a Person Still Has to Decide

show.event: portrait card: What a Person Still Has to Decide

beats.narration_text: Verdict. This document organizes; it doesn't approve. The loop runs end to end on real input, through twelve levels, the guardians and the ending, and through the failures. The rebuild's own levels and layout are labelled. Four defects slipped past the game's own test. What's left is a person's call: the audience, voiced narration, and whether level twelve is fair.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude with your own design document: Here is my game's design document. Pick one proposed experience goal. Rewrite it as a hypothesis with a test I can run with three players, and tell me which result would make me change the design. If no result would change your mind, it isn't a hypothesis yet. Liam, in for Bear.
